team.bio: Taylor is building Baltor to help coding agents work through focused steps with the information, tools and reusable code each step needs. The work combines a hosted intelligence library with a local engine being developed to coordinate a customer's own harnesses and models.
team.basis: The owner supplied this name for the Team page on September 23, 2026. The description draws only on the owner's stated Baltor direction.

posts.title: When a reviewed skill made a model worse
posts.summary: Our first data cleanup study found a phone-number instruction that reduced accuracy. The result changes what we need to check before recommending material.
posts.publication_gate: Before publication, record the affected catalogue item's current disposition and obtain an independent factual review of this article.

blocks.text: A reviewed instruction can still make a task harder. In our first data cleanup study, a cheap cloud model handled phone numbers more accurately without the selected Baltor instruction than with it. We kept the failed runs and changed the homepage example. The result belongs in the product's evidence, alongside the parts that worked.
What we tested

The study used 143 synthetic rows across phone numbers, email addresses, postal addresses and duplicate company records. The phone set contained 38 records. These were constructed test cases, including numbers reserved for fiction, rather than customer data.

Each assignment started a fresh Pi 0.73.1 process. We ran each model and material condition three times per task family. The complete campaign used 72 counted steps and 225 physical model requests within a 400-request ceiling. This was a harness-and-material study, not a full-system benchmark of the complete Baltor design.

The study author constructed this synthetic population and knew the catalogue items. Its challenging cases follow real conventions, and their frequency affects the size of the difference. This is not an estimate of error rates on customer data.
The phone result

With glm-5.3-flash:cloud, phone-record accuracy averaged 99.1 percent without the selected instruction and 84.2 percent with it. The three runs without the instruction passed the task check; none of the three with it passed. The task check required at least 90 percent accuracy and no wrong change to an already correct value.

The instruction relied on a digit-count method that did not handle several cases in this population. It mishandled a United Kingdom trunk-prefix notation, an international dialling prefix and numbers whose apparent length did not make them valid. The model followed that incomplete method instead of applying knowledge that had produced better results without it.
Two failures with different causes

The local qwen2.5-coder:7b model failed earlier in the workflow. It wrote tool requests as plain text, so this version of the harness ended the step without an output file. That is evidence about this model-and-harness connection. It does not establish that local models cannot perform data cleanup.

For the cloud model, more instructions also meant more work. The study recorded more prompt tokens, requests and elapsed time with the material in every family. No task family showed a clear improvement under the study's predeclared comparison rule. Those results do not measure every model, task or possible instruction.
What needs to change

The phone item has been removed from the homepage demonstration. Its catalogue disposition is a separate review decision. A replacement needs tests for the exact failed cases, an explicit scope, and a new comparison using the same task and model conditions. Rewording the item or changing its recorded source revision would not by itself repair the method.

For future recommendations, we need to check that the client can operate its tools, that the selected material reaches the model, and that the resulting work passes an independent task check. A successful download proves receipt of bytes. Tool operation, model use and task acceptance each need their own evidence.

posts.title: What your harness actually reads
posts.summary: A skill can contain instructions, scripts and reference files. Its location and loading rules determine what reaches your agent.
posts.publication_gate: Check linked client guidance against the exact supported versions before publication.

blocks.text: Putting a file in a project directory does not tell you whether an agent read it. Your harness decides which instruction files it loads, where it looks for skills and when it starts a tool. Those rules are part of the connection you need to test.
One skill may contain several files

The Agent Skills format uses a directory with a SKILL.md entry file. That file carries a name and description, followed by instructions. A skill can also include scripts, references and assets. A data-checking skill might pair its instructions with a Python validator and an input schema.

audit-a-data-file/
  SKILL.md
  scripts/check_rows.py
  references/input-schema.json

This is one logical package with three files. The package needs all the files its procedure uses, and each file needs a stable identity. Reviewing the instruction page alone does not establish what the Python code does.
Discovery, loading and use are different

The Agent Skills specification describes loading in stages. A harness can discover a skill's name and description before loading the instructions. It can then read a script or reference when the task needs it. This lets a library hold more material than belongs in one model request.

An installation check should first confirm that the client discovers the selected item. A later observation should show that the content or tool enters the step, and another should show how the agent uses it. The output still needs its own acceptance check. A file can pass the first checks and remain irrelevant to the task.
Use the client's native paths

Different clients have different instruction names, skill directories and trust settings. Some also load material from a home directory or a parent project. A newly created working directory can therefore inherit instructions you did not place there.

For a focused step, start with a named client version, a clear assignment and a recorded set of selected files. Check inherited configuration as well as the new folder. Use the client's documented setup, and test that setup before relying on a filename as evidence of loading.
A file does not grant permission

A script may read data. A configuration may start a process or contact a server. The customer's tool settings and explicit permissions govern those actions. A useful package should explain its inputs, dependencies and effects, so the customer can decide whether it fits the step.

Baltor's hosted service currently searches and delivers a first collection of reviewed Markdown guidance. Complete native multi-file delivery and automatic fresh harnesses for each step are still being built. The design goal is to supply selected material in the form a customer's existing harness can actually use.

posts.title: How we plan a larger harness library
posts.summary: A million files would be useful only if a harness could find a relevant package and use its exact contents. Here is what the count needs to represent.
posts.publication_gate: Update current catalogue facts and review the growth target before publication. Do not present candidates or rendered copies as served inventory.

blocks.text: A developer looking for a procedure does not need a million results. They need one that fits the next step. We want Baltor's library to grow across instructions, skills, tools, reusable code and other files a harness can pick up, while keeping each selection small enough to inspect and use.
Count useful packages and files separately

A skill with an instruction page, a script and a schema contains three files but remains one method. Copies for different clients are delivery variants. A changed title, job label or model-specific wording does not create a new method.

We will need separate counts for candidate material, approved packages, active payload files and client renderings. A source directory can be large while the approved customer library is small. On September 23, the live release still holds 43 approved Markdown items. One million files is a growth goal, not the current inventory.
Start from tasks that need a method

Original procedures can grow from repeated work, verified code, missing search results and task descriptions that have a clear input and output. Occupation data can help identify needs, but changing a job title on the same instructions does not add coverage. The admission process should be able to return no new package when an existing one already fits.

Outside repositories and directories can identify useful work too. Their source, revision and file-level licence need review before copying or redistribution. The official Model Context Protocol Registry describes servers and where to find them; its entries are metadata, not a complete review of the code or remote service they name.
Review the exact thing that will be delivered

Each proposed package needs its complete file list, exact digests, dependencies, allowed use and known failure cases. An independent reviewer should examine the scripts and configuration as well as the prose. Conflicting review decisions need an explicit resolution that names the version and the evidence.

If a file changes, the earlier review must not silently cover the new bytes. If evidence shows that a method fails within its stated scope, that finding must reach the same release and selection process that makes the package available. A successful model vote or a clean format check cannot erase a failed task.
Measure the library as customers experience it

A larger release needs tests for relevance, sensible no-result answers, complete downloads and native loading. It also needs a way to remove an item from future delivery while preserving the historical record. Adding files without those checks would increase the operator's work before it improved the customer's.

The first useful evidence is a small, reviewed release that a customer can search, load and use on a checked step. Growth should preserve that result at each larger size. We will report the count with its definition, release and limits.
